metadata.title: Concepts · LLMS-Explorer
metadata.description: 2347 published references in a map of 2659 topics under 16 roots — generated 2026-11-06.

excerpts.quote: 2347 published references · 312 topic entries · 5006 frontier names · 16 roots · snapshot 2026-11-06 · [3D view](https://llmsx.org/tree/3d/)

A **frontier** name has no topic node of its own. The map derives these names from unresolved `childConcepts` and unchecked entries in the snapshotted research queue. Frontier names indicate work to investigate, not published references. [How to read this](https://llmsx.org/reference/concept-tree/).

**Concepts** is for browsing: click any name to open its children in place and show its facts file in the panel beside the tree. A ● marks a concept with a facts file. The grey count is what opening it reveals: the children drawn directly under it, then every concept below it. Topic groups without facts still open to show their branches. [Research queue](https://llmsx.org/queue/) shows what is being researched now. [Context files](https://llmsx.org/context/) is the other tab: the same concept research as a shelf of facts files to load, sized in tokens.

The [Tessl Registry](https://tessl.co/ctg) already contains review evals for over 2,000 skills, and you can request an evaluation for any public skill here!

**Task evaluations** test the skill’s instructions by running agents with real tasks, with and without the skill, and assessing the results. metadata.ogTitle: Cognition: Auto-Generated Codebase Documentation and Intelligence at Scale - ZenML LLMOps Database
metadata.description: Cognition developed DeepWiki, a system that automatically generates comprehensive documentation for code repositories, initially built to help their AI coding agent Devin understand codebases better. The system addresses the challenge of creating high-quality, scalable documentation for repositories ranging from small projects to enterprise codebases with millions of lines of code across thousands of repositories. By combining heuristic-based file scoring, graph clustering, and agentic LLM orchestration, DeepWiki has indexed 1.4 million repositories and served over 20 million queries. The system evolved from a highly orchestrated approach (v1) to a more agent-driven architecture (v2) that improved quality while reducing costs, demonstrating how improved model capabilities can shift the balance between rigid orchestration and flexible agent autonomy in production LLM systems.
